title: Beyond the 956: Fernando Castillo, vocalist of Los Yaguarú, dies at 72
excerpt: Fernando Castillo Castro, known as Don Fer, a vocalist of the Mexican cumbia group Los Yaguarú de Ángel Venegas, has died at 72. The group announced his death on Friday, October 30, 2026, saying he died the previous day after more than three decades with the band.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Fernando Castillo Castro, known affectionately as Don Fer, a vocalist of the Mexican cumbia group Los Yaguarú de Ángel Venegas, has died at 72.

Castillo died on Thursday, October 29, 2026. His death was announced Friday morning by Los Yaguarú de Ángel Venegas in a statement shared on the group's social media channels, in which his bandmates remembered his talent, his joy, and the legacy he leaves through his songs. No cause of death has been officially reported, and no funeral details have been announced.

"Nos quedamos con tu voz, con los recuerdos, con los escenarios compartidos y con cada momento que hoy adquiere un valor aún más grande," the group wrote. "We keep your voice, the memories, the stages we shared, and every moment that today takes on even greater value."

Born July 5, 1954, Castillo spent more than three decades as a voice of Los Yaguarú de Ángel Venegas, a cumbia group founded in the mid-1990s in central Mexico. His voice carried romantic cumbia recordings including "Pero tu mirada" and "Cuéntale," as well as "Vida no te vayas" and "Como decirte adiós" — songs that made the group a familiar name to fans of Mexican tropical music across the country.

The news of his death was covered across Mexico on Friday, with Milenio and El Universal among the outlets reporting the group's farewell message and the outpouring from fans of the cumbia scene.

Sources: Los Yaguarú de Ángel Venegas (official group statement); Milenio; El Universal; RÉCORD.
